# Detector report (generated by `ml/scripts/train_detector.py`)

> **These numbers come from SYNTHETIC data.** The household behaviour, the sensor noise and the
> fault signatures are simulated by `ml/scripts/generate_data.py`, and the faults are far more
> regular than real plumbing failures. The metrics below will **not** transfer to real sensors
> without recalibration (per-flat baselines from real data, threshold/operating-point tuning and
> a labelled field validation).

- Trained: 2026-10-16T12:07:10+00:00 | seed 42 | sklearn 1.9.1
- Data: 12 flats x 30 days (hash `b2493be28dbd215f`), window = 15
  min, stride 5 min
- Split: chronological, train < 2025-01-27T00:00:00+00:00 (72288 windows) /
  test >= split (31104 windows). Baselines use train-period normal data only;
  IsolationForest (contamination 0.02) fitted on 62874 train-normal windows.
- Selected hyper-parameters (TimeSeriesSplit(3) on train, macro-F1 0.896):
  `{"max_depth": null, "min_samples_leaf": 1, "n_estimators": 100}`

## Held-out test metrics

| class | precision | recall | F1 | support |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| normal | 0.998 | 0.995 | 0.996 | 26176 |
| leak | 0.998 | 0.992 | 0.995 | 4546 |
| burst | 0.968 | 0.953 | 0.961 | 64 |
| overuse | 0.698 | 0.893 | 0.783 | 318 |

- Macro-F1: **0.934**
- Leak+burst recall (any non-normal prediction on a leak/burst window):
  **0.993**
- False-positive rate on normal windows: **0.005**
- Median time-to-detect: 7 min (30/30 test
  episodes detected; measured from true fault onset to first non-normal window)
- IsolationForest on test: flags 2.4% of normal and
  67.6% of fault windows (unsupervised side signal)

Confusion matrix (rows = truth, columns = prediction):

| truth \ pred | normal | leak | burst | overuse |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| normal | 26053 | 5 | 0 | 118 |
| leak | 32 | 4510 | 0 | 4 |
| burst | 2 | 0 | 61 | 1 |
| overuse | 28 | 4 | 2 | 284 |

## Caveats

- Window labels are the fault state at the window end; windows overlap (stride < window), so
  neighbouring test samples are correlated and the effective sample size is small
  (test covers only the last ~30% of days with a handful of fault episodes per flat).
- Slow leaks and drips add a constant floor in a world where normal nights are exactly ~0; real
  households (dripping appliances, filling tanks, pressure cycling) are much noisier.
- Timestamps are treated as UTC; flat-specific timezone handling is the caller's job.
